params.Basis / sources: Healthy 86% at flowering (Jobner field study, RGN-229); 85% max (PLOS ONE 2021 K study). Threshold decline once pustules rupture epidermis (mechanism); your ASD SWIR spectra showed lower water in diseased leaves on 03/03 and 13/03.
Healthy ~72% (similar-experiment HR class; PLOS ONE 2021: 57-73%). Late, steep collapse at high severity (similar-experiment S class 66 -> 31 -> 14%); heat lowers MSI independently.
Healthy 15-20 (similar-experiment HR), 18-31 (Plants 2025, green B. juncea). Chou et al. 2000: whole-leaf A fell to 30% of control by 14 DAI (~30% leaf colonised); decline is non-stomatal.

Healthy 0.38-0.52 (similar-experiment HR); 0.62-0.85 in pots (Plants 2025). Healthy gs declines with VPD (gs_ref x (VPD/1 kPa)^-0.5, Inputs_General). Chou et al. 2000: transpiration unchanged at 8 DAI, so gs declines later and less steeply than Pn.
E = gs x leaf-to-air VPD / P (LI-6400 relation); extra cuticular loss through ruptured pustules. Similar-experiment HR values 4.0-6.6 rising with VPD through the season.

Healthy ~285 (similar-experiment HR). Ci rises while gs falls = non-stomatal limitation (Tatagiba et al. 2015; similar-experiment S class +27%). Not in your list but recorded by the LI-6400 - report it.
Healthy LAI from GDD canopy curve and LAImax per sowing (Inputs_Treatments). Disease: premature senescence and defoliation (Bal & Kumar 2014: total defoliation in unsprayed plots at PDI ~70).

params.Unit: ug mg-1 FW (= mg g-1 FW)
params.Basis / sources: Total chl 0.86-1.75 mg g-1 FW in B. juncea leaves at 45-65 DAS (phytojournal 2019). Chou et al. 2000: chl stable to 12 DAI then -60% in invaded tissue by 14 DAI. Rai et al. 2024: higher in resistant NIL.

params.Unit: ug mg-1 FW (= mg g-1 FW)
params.Basis / sources: a:b ~2.8 in healthy leaves. Chou et al. 2000: both a and b lost. DMSO can overestimate chl b (Quercus study) - use one extraction protocol throughout.
Rai et al. 2024: carotenoids ROSE continuously 0-96 hpi in the susceptible line; field-crop review: Car/Chl rises at intermediate severity. Modelled as small early rise then decline.

No white-rust data at any level. Green B. juncea leaves: anthocyanins near detection limit (PMC4992693). Rise assumed from stress/phenylpropanoid induction (field-crop review); cold (Jan) and senescence also raise it.

Mishra et al. 2009: inoculated leaves 4-10% lower than uninoculated in all 6 genotypes; susceptible genotypes have higher constitutive protein (variety factors). Conversion from %DW (Lowry) to Bradford FW basis is approximate.
